items.content: Microsoft is a technology company dedicated to broadly and responsibly providing digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI). Its mission is to empower every person and organization globally. The company creates AI-powered platforms and tools delivering innovative solutions across infrastructure, data, business applications, and collaboration. Key ambitions include reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud and edge platform, and creating more personal computing. Microsoft offers a range of products and cloud-based services including AI-integrated Microsoft 365, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, Azure AI platform, Windows 11 with AI features, and gaming experiences through Xbox and Activision Blizzard. It emphasizes responsible AI development and sustainability with commitments to carbon negativity and social equity. As of June 30, 2024, Microsoft employed approximately 228,000 people worldwide.

subsections.heading: The Ambitions That Drive Us
subsections.content: Microsoft's research and development efforts focus on three interconnected ambitions: to reinvent productivity and business processes, build the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge platform, and create more personal computing.

subsections.heading: Reinvent Productivity and Business Processes
subsections.content: Key offerings include AI-first Microsoft 365 integrating Office, Windows, Copilot, and security; Microsoft Teams for collaboration; Microsoft Viva for employee experiences; Dynamics 365 as intelligent business applications; role-based Copilots for Sales, Service, and Finance; Copilot Studio for customization; Power Platform for low-code/no-code tools; LinkedIn with AI-enabled insights transforming professional interactions.

subsections.heading: Build the Intelligent Cloud and Intelligent Edge Platform
subsections.content: Microsoft focuses on digital transformation across sectors, investing in high-performance and sustainable computing with a global datacenter network. Azure offers hybrid cloud capabilities, developer productivity, data and AI features, and trusted security. The company provides purpose-built cloud infrastructure including custom AI accelerator Azure Maia and CPU Azure Cobalt. Azure AI supports organizations with frontier models, tooling, and infrastructure, deploying Copilot stack widely and advancing AI responsibly. GitHub Copilot aids AI-powered software development. Microsoft is the exclusive cloud provider for OpenAI and deeply integrated with its research.

subsections.heading: Create More Personal Computing
subsections.content: Microsoft advances computing with Windows 11 featuring performance and AI innovations like Copilot, secure privacy features, and developer tools. Devices include Surface and Copilot+ PCs with on-device AI. Microsoft Edge browser and AI-powered Bing with Copilot enhance user experience. The company expands gaming through Xbox hardware, cloud services, Xbox Game Pass subscription, and content via acquisition of Activision Blizzard.

subsections.heading: Gaming
subsections.content: Microsoft expands global access to gaming across PC, console, mobile, and cloud, investing in studios and leveraging Xbox Game Pass subscription. The gamer is central to the ecosystem, with focus on exclusive content, device computational power, and growing platforms including first- and third-party content.

subsections.heading: Our Future Opportunity
subsections.content: Microsoft aims to lead in AI and cloud solutions driving digital transformation, modern business applications, enhanced security, innovative gaming, and growth in PC market share through engagement with services like Microsoft Edge, Bing, Teams, Microsoft 365 Consumer, and Xbox Game Pass.

subsections.heading: Corporate Social Responsibility - Commitment to Sustainability
subsections.content: Microsoft committed in 2020 to be carbon negative, water positive, and zero waste by 2030. Progress includes reducing operational emissions, accelerating carbon removal, designing for circularity, and improving biodiversity. Challenges remain in reducing indirect emissions and water use. New technologies like generative AI pose opportunities and infrastructure challenges.

subsections.heading: Addressing Racial Injustice and Inequity
subsections.content: Since 2020, Microsoft has made multi-year commitments to address racial injustice and inequity affecting racial and ethnic minorities in the U.S. Programs support over 3,000 organizations in Black and African American communities, expanded educational initiatives like TEALS, and invested $150 million in minority-owned institutions and small businesses. The company aims to double Black, African American, Hispanic, and Latinx leadership by 2025.

subsections.heading: Investing in Digital Skills
subsections.content: The Skills for Jobs initiative supports a skills-based labor market, surpassing goals with 12.6 million trained by May 2024. A U.S. cybersecurity workforce campaign aims to train 250,000 by 2025, with expanded global efforts. The AI Skills initiative launched in 2023 promotes generative AI learning, grants, and digital resources reaching over 2.5 million people worldwide by June 2024.

subsections.heading: HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
subsections.content: Microsoft employs about 228,000 full-time people globally as of June 30, 2024, across operations, product development, sales, marketing, and administration. The company fosters a growth mindset culture focused on inclusion, security, and collaboration, enabling employees to create innovative products and services.

subsections.heading: OPERATING SEGMENTS
subsections.content: Microsoft organizes reporting into three main segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. These segments align strategies, resources, and provide comprehensive financial views of key businesses.

subsections.heading: Productivity and Business Processes
subsections.content: This segment includes productivity, communication, and information services: Office Commercial and Consumer offerings, LinkedIn with its Talent, Marketing, Sales, and Premium services, and Dynamics business solutions including cloud and on-premises ERP, CRM, Power Apps, and Power Automate. Growth drivers include installed user base, subscription shifts, AI integration, and expansion in new markets.

subsections.heading: Competition (Productivity and Business Processes)
subsections.content: Microsoft competes with companies like Apple, Cisco, Google, Meta, Slack, Zoom, and various security, collaboration, and professional network providers. Competition arises from software vendors, application developers, marketplaces, and others providing security, advertising, and content solutions. The company differentiates through integrated, secure, flexible, and comprehensive products that work well on-premises and in the cloud.

subsections.heading: Intelligent Cloud
subsections.content: This segment includes Azure and other cloud services, server products, developer tools, Nuance healthcare and enterprise AI solutions, and GitHub platform services. Enterprise and Partner services provide support, solutions, and training. Azure offers hybrid cloud, AI-optimized infrastructure, and developer productivity. The cloud faces competition from Amazon, Google, IBM, Oracle, and open source alternatives.

subsections.heading: More Personal Computing
subsections.content: This segment consists of Windows (OEM licensing, commercial licenses, cloud services), Devices (Surface, HoloLens, and accessories), Gaming (Xbox hardware, content, subscriptions, cloud gaming, Activision Blizzard), and Search and news advertising (Bing, Microsoft Edge, Microsoft News). Windows competes on device volume, pricing, AI features, and customer mix. Device growth depends on PC shipments and innovation.

items.content: Microsoft's gaming platform provides entertainment via content, community, and cloud services. It develops first-party games and invests in studios to expand intellectual property. Xbox Game Pass offers access to over 400 titles. The platform supports gaming across consoles, Windows devices, and others. Growth depends on active user base, game availability, exclusive content, device performance, and new experience creation.

subsections.heading: Competition
subsections.content: Xbox and cloud gaming face competition from Amazon, Apple, Meta, Tencent, Nintendo, Sony, video streaming services, and other entertainment providers. Microsoft's platform differentiates through hardware architecture, user interface, developer tools, online services, and strong first-party content.

items.content: Microsoft delivers search, native, and display advertising globally via Bing with Copilot, Microsoft Edge, and partnerships like Yahoo. Growth depends on attracting new users, understanding intent, and matching ads to relevant content.

subsections.heading: Competition
subsections.content: The search and news advertising business competes with Google, OpenAI, Meta, and various websites, social platforms, and content portals.

items.content: Microsoft operates regional service centers supporting contract processing, billing, credit, collections, lifecycle operations, and logistics across Africa, Europe, Middle East, Asia-Pacific, and Americas. Datacenters are located globally with plans to expand capacity to meet AI demands. Devices are manufactured by third-party contractors with backup suppliers available, but some components have limited suppliers which could impact manufacturing timing.

Microsoft develops products internally through engineering groups focusing on cloud and AI, strategic missions like quantum computing, user experiences and devices, Microsoft AI, security, technology and research, LinkedIn, and gaming. Internal development sustains competitive advantage and product quality. The company prepares vendors with resources ahead of platform releases to aid compatibility and development.

items.item_title: Product and Service Development, and Intellectual Property
items.content: Microsoft protects its intellectual property through enforcement of copyright, trademark, and trade secrets globally. It holds over 63,000 patents issued and licenses technology both inbound and outbound. Sometimes, Microsoft provides IP broadly at no or low cost to support standards and open source. The company believes licenses are generally obtainable on commercially reasonable terms. Its ongoing R&D is not materially dependent on any single license or agreement.

Microsoft invests significantly in emerging technologies including cloud computing, AI, devices, and operating systems, supporting fundamental research and coordinating R&D across segments to maintain innovation and competitive positioning.

Microsoft markets and distributes products through OEMs, direct sales, and distributors/resellers globally. The sales organization works with enterprises, public sectors, OEMs, partners, and resellers to fulfill customer digital transformation needs. Various channels target diverse customer segments with support and training.

Microsoft offers volume licensing programs for organizations of different sizes, such as Enterprise Agreement, Microsoft Customer Agreement, Online Subscription Agreement, Microsoft Products and Services Agreement, Open Value, Select Plus, and partner programs. Software Assurance provides rights to upgrades and support. Cloud Solution Provider and Services Provider programs facilitate cloud service licensing and hosted applications.

Microsoft serves individual consumers, small to medium organizations, large global enterprises, public-sector institutions, ISPs, developers, and OEMs. The company ships products promptly, resulting in minimal backlog.

Microsoft is subject to diverse and evolving global laws and regulations related to its products and services, including privacy, telecommunications, data protection, advertising, and content. It has established a regulatory governance framework focused on Responsible AI, Privacy, Digital Safety, and Cybersecurity to maintain compliance, customer trust, and scale regulatory capabilities. Specific compliance functions exist to meet regulations like the EU Digital Markets and Services Acts. Regulatory risks are described further in Risk Factors.

As of July 30, 2024, Microsoft's executive officers include Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella (56), EVP and Chief Commercial Officer Judson B. Althoff (51), EVP and Chief Human Resources Officer Kathleen T. Hogan (58), EVP and Chief Financial Officer Amy E. Hood (52), EVP and Chief Marketing Officer Takeshi Numoto (53), Vice Chair and President Bradford L. Smith (65), and EVP Business Development, Strategy, and Ventures Christopher D. Young (52). Their backgrounds and appointments are described, including prior roles and board memberships.

Microsoft's operations face risks including intense competition across markets and technology sectors, rapid industry evolution with frequent product introductions, and competitive platform-based ecosystems. The business faces pressures from cloud-based and AI services markets with high development costs. Risks from new business models, including free and open source offerings, require innovation and responsiveness. Execution challenges in cloud and AI service growth, security threats, and regulatory developments may adversely affect operations and financial condition.

subsections.heading: Cybersecurity, Data Privacy, and Platform Abuse Risks
subsections.content: Threat actors including state-sponsored groups conduct attacks via malware, exploiting vulnerabilities, social engineering, and supply chain risks. Microsoft has experienced incidents like a nation-state password spray attack in late 2023 resulting in unauthorized access to email and source code. Cyber threats continuously evolve with emerging technologies like AI, complicating defenses. Breaches may cause reputational harm, service disruptions, increased costs, legal/regulatory risk, and operational challenges. Security controls and monitoring are ongoing priorities.

items.item_title: Risks Relating to the Evolution of Our Business
items.content: Microsoft invests heavily in new products, services, and technologies, including AI and hardware, with associated risks of delayed or unsuccessful commercialization, potential negative public perception, and regulatory challenges. Acquisitions such as those of Nuance Communications and Activision Blizzard involve operational and integration risks. Goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges are possible from such transactions. The company faces various operational, legal, and market risks that could adversely impact financial results.

items.item_title: Cybersecurity, Data Privacy, and Platform Abuse Risks
items.content: Microsoft recognizes cybersecurity as a critical risk area with incidents including sophisticated, persistent attacks by nation-state actors, exploiting software and hardware vulnerabilities, social engineering, and internal account security failures. These incidents can lead to reputational damage, financial loss, regulatory challenges, and service impairments. The evolving threat landscape includes new AI-powered attack methods. Defense strategies require continuous improvement, employee training, and incident response capability.

subsections.heading: Security of our Information Technology
subsections.content: Threats come from hackers, nation-states, and groups using varied methods like malware, exploiting vulnerabilities, social engineering, and supply chain attacks. A notable incident in late 2023 involved compromise of Microsoft email and source code. Cyber threats are increasingly complex and may evade detection, potentially causing operational and reputational harm.

items.content: Microsoft has received no written comments from SEC staff regarding its periodic or current reports, issued more than 180 days before the end of fiscal year 2024, that remain unresolved.

Microsoft prioritizes cybersecurity, launching the Secure Future Initiative (SFI) in November 2023 and expanding it in May 2024, focusing on Secure by Design, Secure by Default, and Secure Operations principles. The Board of Directors provides oversight with quarterly reviews, supported by senior management presentations. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) leads cybersecurity strategy and operations, with executive-level support from the Cybersecurity Governance Council (CGC). Microsoft invests heavily in security awareness, monitoring, and response to evolving cyber threats.

subsections.heading: Risk Management and Strategy
subsections.content: Microsoft's corporate priority is protecting customer and employee digital environments through continuous improvement in cybersecurity protections, aligned with three principles: Secure by Design, Secure by Default, and Secure Operations.

subsections.heading: Governance
subsections.content: Cybersecurity oversight is conducted by the Board of Directors with scheduled reviews. Presentations by senior management including the CISO and EVP of Security inform the Board of threats, incidents, security risks, and remediation efforts. The Cybersecurity Governance Council supports governance, risk assessment, and compliance activities.

items.item_title: Market For Registrant’s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters, and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities
items.content: Microsoft's common stock trades on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT. As of July 25, 2024, there were 81,346 registered holders. In the Q4 fiscal 2024, Microsoft repurchased approximately 7 million shares monthly, totaling $11.96 billion in buybacks for fiscal year 2024. The Board declared quarterly dividends of $0.75 per share amounting to $22.3 billion in fiscal year 2024. Total returns to shareholders in Q4 fiscal 2024 were $8.4 billion through buybacks and dividends.

items.item_title: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
items.content: Microsoft's investments are predominantly Level 1 or Level 2, priced by vendors or brokers with active markets or observable inputs, subject to controls like model validation and periodic review. Cash from operations was $118.5 billion in fiscal 2024, an increase of $31.0 billion primarily from customer receipts. Financing cash outflows decreased by $6.2 billion, reflecting reduced stock repurchases and increased debt issuance. Investing cash outflows increased by $74.3 billion due mainly to acquisitions and property and equipment additions. Microsoft issues debt for corporate purposes including capital and acquisitions. Unearned revenue largely stems from volume licensing and cloud services, recognized ratably over contract terms totaling $60.184 billion as of June 30, 2024.

subsections.heading: Material Cash Requirements and Other Obligations
subsections.content: As of June 30, 2024, Microsoft’s contractual obligations total approximately $360 billion, including long-term debt principal ($48.971 billion) and interest ($27.041 billion), construction commitments ($35.391 billion), operating and finance leases ($172.725 billion), and purchase commitments ($72.022 billion). The company pays a transition tax over eight years totaling $7.6 billion remaining as of June 30, 2024. Share repurchases totaled 32 million shares for $12.0 billion in 2024 (69 million shares for $18.4 billion in 2023). Dividends paid were $22.3 billion for fiscal 2024. Planned capital expenditures include investments in cloud, AI infrastructure, acquisitions, and data centers.

items.content: Microsoft reports fair value of derivatives, with gross derivative assets and liabilities subject to netting of $304 million and $800 million as of June 30, 2024, respectively. Inventories totaled $1.246 billion as of June 30, 2024. Property and equipment at cost was $212 billion with net value $135.6 billion as of June 30, 2024, including $35.4 billion committed for construction. Activision Blizzard acquisition purchase price was approximately $75.4 billion, with $51.0 billion goodwill assigned to More Personal Computing segment. Intangible assets amortization expense was $4.8 billion in fiscal 2024. Long-term debt included $3.6 billion related to Activision Blizzard acquisition. No goodwill impairment was identified in 2024. Deferred income tax assets and liabilities, income tax components and effective tax rate reconciliation are also reported.

subsections.heading: NOTE 6 — INVENTORIES
subsections.content: Inventories consist of raw materials ($394 million), work in process ($7 million), and finished goods ($845 million) as of June 30, 2024.

subsections.heading: NOTE 7 — PROPERTY AND EQUIPMENT
subsections.content: Property and equipment totaled $212 billion at cost and $135.6 billion net as of June 30, 2024, with $15.2 billion depreciation expense in fiscal 2024. Construction commitments were $35.4 billion.

subsections.heading: NOTE 8 — BUSINESS COMBINATIONS
subsections.content: The Activision Blizzard acquisition was preliminarily allocated with $12.976 billion cash, $50.969 billion goodwill, and $21.969 billion intangible assets. The acquisition impacts and pro forma consolidated results are described. Nuance Communications acquisition goodwill was assigned to Intelligent Cloud.

subsections.heading: NOTE 9 — GOODWILL
subsections.content: Goodwill totaled $119.2 billion as of June 30, 2024, with $51.0 billion related to Activision Blizzard. No impairment was identified in 2024.

subsections.heading: NOTE 10 — INTANGIBLE ASSETS
subsections.content: Intangible assets amortization expense was $4.8 billion in 2024. Future amortization expense estimates are provided.

subsections.heading: NOTE 11 — DEBT
subsections.content: Short-term commercial paper outstanding was $6.7 billion at 5.4% interest as of June 30, 2024. Long-term debt includes $3.6 billion related to Activision Blizzard. Interest paid was $1.7 billion in fiscal 2024.

subsections.heading: NOTE 12 — INCOME TAXES
subsections.content: Provision for income taxes components, income before tax by geography, and effective tax rate reconciliations are reported. Unrecognized tax benefits totaled $22.8 billion as of June 30, 2024, with associated accrued interest and audit information.

items.content: Microsoft holds operating and finance leases for data centers, offices, research facilities, Experience Centers, and equipment, with lease terms up to 17 years and options to extend or terminate leases. Lease expense in fiscal 2024 was approximately $6.1 billion. Additional lease liabilities total $127 billion for uncommenced leases. The company is involved in litigation alleging cell phone radiation caused health effects, with ongoing appeals. The Irish Data Protection Commission has investigated LinkedIn's targeted advertising under GDPR, with draft decisions pending. Microsoft accrues for other contingent liabilities and estimates potential adverse impacts. The Board has approved share repurchase programs with ongoing dividends, returning significant capital to shareholders.

subsections.heading: Lease Expense and Cash Flows
subsections.content: Fiscal 2024 operating lease cost was $3.555 billion; finance lease amortization and interest totaled $2.534 billion. Cash flows reflect payments related to these leases and assets obtained in exchange for lease obligations.

subsections.heading: Contingencies and Litigation
subsections.content: Ongoing litigation includes 45 lawsuits alleging cell phone radiation health effects; the company has moved to exclude plaintiff expert evidence. LinkedIn is subject to GDPR investigation by IDPC. Management estimates $641 million liability accrual, with possible additional material impacts.

subsections.heading: Stockholders' Equity and Share Repurchases
subsections.content: Outstanding shares decreased by 32 million in 2024 with active repurchase programs authorized up to $60 billion. Dividends declared totaled $22.3 billion in fiscal 2024.

items.content: Management, including the CEO and CFO, evaluated Microsoft's disclosure controls and procedures as of fiscal year-end 2024, concluding they are effective. The internal control over financial reporting was assessed using COSO framework, excluding the recent Activision Blizzard acquisition controls which comprise less than 1% of total assets and 2% of revenue. No material weaknesses were identified or changes that would materially affect control effectiveness. Deloitte & Touche LLP audited the internal control effective as of June 30, 2024, and issued an unqualified opinion.

subsections.heading: Report of Management on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting
subsections.content: Management is responsible for internal controls to ensure reliable financial reporting. Evaluations concluded controls are effective with inherent limitations.

subsections.heading: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
subsections.content: Deloitte & Touche LLP audited the internal controls and financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, expressing an unqualified opinion on both and noting exclusion of Activision Blizzard controls from scope due to acquisition timing and immateriality.

items.content: During the three months ended June 30, 2024, no officers or directors adopted, modified, or terminated any Rule 10b5-1 trading plans or comparable non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangements.

items.item_title: Directors, Executive Officers, and Corporate Governance
items.content: Information on executive officers is provided in Part I, Item 1. Details about directors, Audit Committee, and corporate governance are available in the Proxy Statement for the December 2024 Annual Meeting, incorporated by reference. Microsoft has adopted a Finance Code of Professional Conduct, insider trading policies including a General Insider Trading Policy, Restricted Trading Window Policy, and insider trading compliance policies for officers and directors. These policies are publicly available and promote compliance with laws and listing standards.
Information regarding Director and Named Executive Officer compensation, Compensation Committee activities, and insider participation is incorporated by reference from the Proxy Statement.

items.item_title: Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder Matters
items.content: Information on stock ownership of beneficial owners, principal shareholders, and equity compensation plans is incorporated by reference from the Proxy Statement.

items.item_title: Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence
items.content: Information on director independence and related party transactions is incorporated by reference from the Proxy Statement.

Details on fees paid to principal accountant Deloitte & Touche LLP and policy on audit committee pre-approval of audit and permissible non-audit services are incorporated by reference from the Proxy Statement.
Financial statements are provided in Part II, Item 8. Financial statement schedules have been omitted as they are either not required, not applicable, or information is included elsewhere.
None.
